newsitem.title: USA: CNG adds 270 bln cubic ft to reserves.
newsitem.headline: CNG adds 270 bln cubic ft to reserves.

text.p: Consolidated Natural Gas Co said Friday it added more than 270 billion cubic feet equivalent to proven reserves 1996, the since 1985.
This equalled about 159 percent of oil and natural gas production, the third straight year CNG's reserve additions have exceeded production, the company said.

At year end, CNG said, its total reserves were almost 1.4 trillion cubic feet equivalent, up from 1.3 trillion cubic feet equivalent at the end of 1995. The 1996 reserve total includes over 1 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 50 million barrels of oil.
Over the past three years, it noted, reserve additions from drilling, revisions and purchases have equalled about 175 percent of production.

The company said its fove-year average finding and development costs have declined to about $0.75 per thousand cubic feet equivalent. Included in the reserve additions are major discoveries in the Main Pass and West Cameron areas of the Gulf of Mexico and 47 billion cubic feet equivalent of reserves obtained through acquisitions in Utah.

For the second straight year, CNG said, its reserve additions were balanced, with half of the reserves coming from its traditional strength, the shallower water of the Gulf of Mexico, and the remainder from onshore projects, acquisitions and deepwater projects.

CNG produced more than 170 billion cubic feet equivalent in 1996. Major contributors were two new Gulf of Mexico fields -- Popeye, a deepwater project that produced 28 billion cubic feet equivalent, and Main Pass, which produced 14 billion.
